parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is documented, and same-sex conduct is legal, so the sexuality statute is not the driver. The main traveller-relevant evidence is police behaviour: a May 2026 raid on an LGBTQ+ venue detained about 30 people, with alleged warrantless entry, extortion and a baseless charge. That is state-directed targeting of sexual minorities, which may extend to visibly trans visitors. Reporting of intensified persecution after the disputed 2024 election is undated and unquantified, but adds a state-climate signal. There is no hate-crime or gender-identity anti-discrimination law and no documented remedy. Visitor-facing trans exposures (border marker checks, facility rules, custody placement, emergency care) are undocumented, so I extrapolated from the criminalisation-free but thin-remedy structure and the extortion record. Positives: a majority public supports equal rights, a trans candidate ran, and a court ruling protects families. Overall, Elevated Risk.
